¿Qué factores llevaron a que Arequipa tenga un mayor nivel de congestión vehicular que Lima?

2026-08-27 El Comercio Perú TomTom Traffic Index, Arequipa, Lima, Peru, traffic congestion, urban mobility, GPS navigation, congestion level, 154 hours
Read the source article

Quick summary

TomTom's latest Traffic Index reveals that Arequipa, Peru's second-largest city, has surpassed Lima in congestion level at 69.5%, with drivers losing 154 hours per year in traffic — raising questions about urban planning in rapidly growing secondary cities.

Key takeaways

  • Arequipa ranks 8th globally in TomTom's Traffic Index with a 69.5% congestion level, higher than Lima's 69.3%
  • Drivers in Arequipa lost an average of 154 hours in traffic during 2025 — equivalent to 6 days and 10 hours
  • Arequipa's congestion worsened by 1.9 percentage points from 2024, while Lima's increased by 0.8 points
  • Despite having less total time lost than Lima (154 vs 195 hours), Arequipa's congestion percentage is higher due to its smaller road network
  • TomTom monitors traffic in 500 cities worldwide using anonymised GPS data from drivers across the complete road network
